title: Directed unions assemble coherent colimits without cocompleteness
statement:
Use the universes, simplicial subsets, nerves, quasicategories, coherent diagrams, mapping spaces and cocones of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Let $I$ be a small nonempty partially ordered set in which every finite subset has an upper bound. Let $(K_i)_{i\in I}$ be an increasing family of simplicial subsets of a small simplicial set $K$, with $K=\bigcup_iK_i$. Let $p:K\to\mathcal E$ be a diagram in a quasicategory, and choose for each $i$ a colimiting cocone $\lambda_i:p|_{K_i}\to\Delta_{K_i}c_i$.

The chosen local colimits admit a coherent assembly $c:N(I)\to\mathcal E$, with vertices $c_i$ and transitions induced by restriction of the chosen cocones, together with equivalences, natural in $t\in\mathcal E$,
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(N(I),\mathcal E)}(c,\Delta_{N(I)}t)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal E)}(p,\Delta_Kt).$$
The equivalences identify a cocone on $c$ with the compatible cocone on $p$ obtained by composing its legs with the $\lambda_i$. In particular, a cocone on $c$ is colimiting if and only if the corresponding cocone on $p$ is colimiting. No colimits in $\mathcal E$ other than the displayed local ones are assumed. For any quasicategory $\mathcal E'$, if a coherent functor $H:\mathcal E\to\mathcal E'$ sends every $\lambda_i$ to a colimiting cocone, the image assembly $Hc$ is an assembly for $Hp$ and the comparison of cocones commutes with $H$, up to coherent equivalence, using those image cocones. The assertion includes empty $K$ and empty $K_i$.

source.place: Proposition 4.2.3.4, Remark 4.2.3.9 and Corollary 4.2.3.10, printed pp. 249-253: local colimit comparison for a directed covering by simplicial subsets. Read online 2026-10-17; not archived in literature/ (WANTED). No Stacks tag states this quasicategorical result.

proof.text: Form the following small simplicial subset $M\subseteq K\star N(I)$. It contains $K$ and $N(I)$; a mixed simplex is a simplex $\sigma$ of $K$ followed by a chain $i_0\leq\cdots\leq i_r$, and belongs to $M$ exactly when $\sigma\in K_{i_0}$. Deleting initial chain vertices preserves membership by monotonicity, and all other operators preserve it because every $K_i$ is a simplicial subset. In particular $K_i\star\{i\}$ is the right cone on $K_i$. Replace each chosen coherent cocone by a join representative on this right cone. The fixed-boundary, fixed-vertex comparison in the cited join-cone lemma (applied to opposites) supplies these representatives with their specified equivalences to the chosen cocones; their vertices are still $c_i$. For the subset functor $F:i\mapsto(K_i\hookrightarrow K)$, this $M$ is exactly the simplicial set $K_F$ defined in [lem-coef-decomposition-local-colimit-cocones]: a compatible family of lifts of a lower simplex is uniquely determined by its membership in $K_{i_0}$. This identifies every pure and mixed summand and all their operators, not merely the vertices.

Construct $q:M\to\mathcal E$ with $q|_K=p$ by adjoining the nondegenerate simplices of $N(I)$ in increasing dimension, and well ordering the simplices within each dimension. At a vertex $i$ attach the chosen map on $K_i\star\{i\}$. At a positive-dimensional chain $\tau=(i_0<\cdots<i_n)$, the new part is the pushout attachment of $K_{i_0}\star\Delta^n$ along $K_{i_0}\star\partial\Delta^n$: the map $K_{i_0}\star\Delta^n\to M$ is injective because $\tau$ is, the simplices over $\tau$ itself are new, and the old simplices it meets are exactly those of $K_{i_0}\star\partial\Delta^n$ (old simplices $\sigma\star\rho$ with $\rho$ in the face omitting $i_0$ and $\sigma\in K_{i_1}\setminus K_{i_0}$ are not in its image). Its faces already occur, including its first-vertex cone, which is the chosen colimiting representative on $p|_{K_{i_0}}$. To extend over this cell, write $a=p|_{K_{i_0}}$ and let $J_a$ be the join slice of [lem-coef-join-slice-cocone-comparison], whose $m$-simplices are the maps $K_{i_0}\star\Delta^m\to\mathcal E$ restricting to $a$. Since $K_{i_0}\star\partial\Delta^n$ is degreewise the union of the simplicial subsets $K_{i_0}\star\Delta^{F}$ over the proper faces $F$, with $K_{i_0}\star\Delta^F\cap K_{i_0}\star\Delta^{F'}=K_{i_0}\star\Delta^{F\cap F'}$, the map already given on $K_{i_0}\star\partial\Delta^n$ is exactly a map $b:\partial\Delta^n\to J_a$, and an extension over $K_{i_0}\star\Delta^n$ fixing it is exactly an extension of $b$ to $\Delta^n$. By [lem-coef-join-slice-cocone-comparison], $J_a$ is a quasicategory (it is functor-equivalent to the cocone category) and its vertex $b(0)$ is initial, because its associated coherent cocone, read through $K_{i_0}\times\Delta^1\to K_{i_0}\star\Delta^0$, is the chosen colimiting cocone. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-relative-initial-boundary] to the inner fibration $J_a\to\Delta^0$: $\operatorname{Map}_{\Delta^0}$ is a point, so being initial relative to $J_a\to\Delta^0$ means being initial, and its boundary-filling condition for $n\geq1$, applied to the boundary map $b$ with first vertex $b(0)$ and the unique map $\Delta^n\to\Delta^0$, extends $b$ to $\Delta^n$ with the entire boundary fixed. This includes $K_{i_0}=\varnothing$, where $J_a=\mathcal E$ and $b(0)=c_{i_0}$ is initial. At a limit ordinal take the union of the already agreeing simplicial maps, degree by degree. Every simplex occurs, so this constructs $q$ on all of $M$. Put $c=q|_{N(I)}$. The triangle on a simplex of $K_i$ followed by $i\leq j$ identifies the leg to $c_j$ with its composite through $c_i$; longer chains give the required higher compatibilities. Thus the transitions are induced by restriction of the chosen cocones.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 4.2.3.4, the induction on simplices of N(I): extension of a boundary in the cocone quasicategory from its initial first vertex

proof.text:
Apply [lem-coef-decomposition-local-colimit-cocones] to the small ordinary category $I$, its subset functor $F$ and the particular extension $q$ of step 2. Its local cone $q\iota_i$ is the chosen colimiting join representative on $K_i\star\{i\}$, so its only local-colimit hypothesis holds for every $i$. The identification $M=K_F$ in step 1 identifies its actual restriction map with
$$\alpha_t:\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(M,\mathcal E)}(q,\Delta_Mt)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal E)}(p,\Delta_Kt).$$
The cited statement makes this an equivalence, natural in $t$ and compatible with coherent postcomposition of cocones. Its hypotheses explicitly allow arbitrary simplicial subsets, including empty ones, and assume no colimits beyond the displayed local cocones.

source.place: Proposition 4.2.3.4, last assertion, printed pp.249-251; coherent-cocone formulation of the cited existing node.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-directed-decomposition-right-anodyne] to $I$ and the same family. Its hypotheses are exactly the given smallness, nonemptiness, finite upper bounds, monotonicity and degreewise covering. The degreewise formula for its $K_F$ agrees with $M$: a mixed simplex is a lower simplex in the first indexed subset followed by an upper chain. The face deleting the first upper vertex uses precisely $K_{i_0}\subseteq K_{i_1}$. Thus its conclusion gives that $N(I)\hookrightarrow M$ is right anodyne. Neither the indexing subsets nor $M$ is being assumed a quasicategory.

source.place: Proposition 4.2.3.8 and Remark 4.2.3.9, printed p.252; existing directed-subset specialization.

proof.text:
Apply right-anodyne cocone restriction to $N(I)\hookrightarrow M$ and $q$. It gives a natural equivalence
$$\beta_t:\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(M,\mathcal E)}(q,\Delta_Mt)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(N(I),\mathcal E)}(c,\Delta_{N(I)}t).$$
The span $\alpha_t\beta_t^{-1}$ is the claimed equivalence, natural in $t$. Inversion is coherent because a transformation of space-valued diagrams whose components are equivalences is an equivalence, by the cited functor-cone calculus. The comparison of legs is explicit: restrict a cocone on $q$ to $K_i\star\{i\}$; its mixed triangles identify the leg on $p|_{K_i}$ with $p|_{K_i}\xrightarrow{\lambda_i}c_i\to t$. These triangles and all higher mixed simplices give compatibility on overlaps. The equivalence $\beta_t$ says every cocone on $c$ admits just this extension up to a contractible space of choices.

source.place: Corollary 4.2.3.10, with its two restriction maps

proof.text: For corresponding cocones with apex $x$, their maps from $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(x,t)$ to the two spaces of $t$-valued cocones agree under the comparison: both postcompose their legs by $x\to t$. The dual cone criterion in the functor-cone calculus says either cocone is colimiting exactly when all these maps are equivalences. Since the two target spaces are naturally equivalent, the criteria agree.

source.place: Corollary 4.2.3.10, colimit identification by universal properties

proof.text: Finally use $Hq:M\to\mathcal E'$ and the same simplicial collage. Its local cone maps are the images of the chosen ones and are colimiting by the stated hypothesis. Thus [lem-coef-decomposition-local-colimit-cocones] gives the counterpart of $\alpha$ for $Hq$, while the right-anodyne inclusion from step 4 and [lem-coef-infinity-anodyne-cocones] give the counterpart of $\beta$. Postcomposition sends the restriction span $(\alpha_t,\beta_t)$ to that span for $Hq$ and $H(t)$: both squares commute because restriction and postcomposition commute as simplicial maps. Their inverses therefore commute up to coherent equivalence. The local-cone representatives are also carried to representatives of the image cocones, since the join-to-transformation map is fixed on the indexing sets. This proves functor compatibility with assembly $Hc$. If $K_i$ is empty the required local cocone is an initial object and the cell extension of step 2 still applies, with $J_a=\mathcal E$. If $K$ is empty, then every $K_i$ is empty and $M=N(I)$; the right-anodyne comparison is the identity, and the first restriction equivalence compares with the one-point space of empty cocones. Hence both empty cases are included and only the displayed local colimits have been used.
